item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00089","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C01","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 is a near-complete drafting template for the child: both are letters to the same Attorney General, open by recounting creation of a section 206 Board of Inquiry, note receipt and attachment of its report, make the same statutory finding about an unresolved strike affecting a substantial interstate industry and imperiling national health and safety, and conclude with virtually identical section 208 instructions to petition a federal district court for an injunction and other appropriate relief. The child principally substitutes the copper-industry parties and factual details and adjusts singular terms to multiple disputes, strikes, or lockouts. C01 and C06 use the same machinery and sequence but are less proximate matches than C25.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"On August 30, 1951, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 (Public Law 101, 80th Congress), I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in labor disputes...","parent_excerpt":"On February 6, 1950, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 (Public Law 101, 80th Congress), I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in a labor dispute...","explanation":"The opening sentence shares the same statute citation, authority formula, prior-directive reference, and Board-of-Inquiry construction, with the industry and parties replaced."},{"child_excerpt":"On September 4, 1951, I received the Board's written report in the matter. A copy of that report is attached hereto.","parent_excerpt":"On February 11, 1950, I received the Board's written report in the matter, including a statement of the facts with respect to the dispute and each party's statement of its position. A copy of that report is attached hereto.","explanation":"Both next record receipt of the Board's report on the date of the letter and attach it."},{"child_excerpt":"In my opinion, these unresolved labor disputes have resulted in strikes or lock-outs affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several States and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce, which strikes or lock-outs, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.","parent_excerpt":"In my opinion this unresolved labor dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several States and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.","explanation":"This is distinctive, nearly verbatim statutory-finding language, modified chiefly for multiple disputes and possible lockouts."},{"child_excerpt":"I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, to petition in the name of the United States any District Court of the United States having jurisdiction of the parties to enjoin the continuance of such strikes or lock-outs where such action is necessary to secure a resumption of production in the industry, and for such relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","parent_excerpt":"I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, to petition in the name of the United States any district court of the United States having jurisdiction of the parties to enjoin the continuance of such strike, and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","explanation":"The operative instruction reproduces the same section 208 injunction machinery and much of the wording, adding only a copper-production qualification and pluralization."}]}
